questions: If multiple positions in S match T, which (a, b) should be output – the smallest row index, then smallest column, or any matching position?
Are the coordinates (a, b) 1‑based or 0‑based in the output?
Must the pattern T match exactly, or are rotations/reflections of T also considered a match?
Should the program treat the input lines for S and T as having no spaces between characters, and are there any trailing spaces to ignore?
Is it guaranteed that at least one occurrence of T exists in S, or should we handle the case where there is none (and if so, what output is required)?
Are N and M given on the same line separated by a space, and can there be extra whitespace before or after them?
Can N or M be equal to 0, or are they strictly positive integers?
Are there any limits on the total size of the input (e.g., line length) that could affect reading the grids?

inline_prompts: You are given an N \times N grid S and an M \times M grid T. The cell at the i-th row from the top and the j-th column from the left is denoted by (i,j). The colors of the cells in S and T are represented by N^2 characters S_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq N) and M^2 characters T_{i,j} (1\leq i,j\leq M), respectively. In grid S, cell (i,j) is white if S_{i,j} is ., and black if S_{i,j} is #. The same applies for grid T. Find T within S. The match must be exact, with every cell of T must exactly match; rotations/reflections are not allowed. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N M S_{1,1}S_{1,2}\dots S_{1,N} S_{2,1}S_{2,2}\dots S_{2,N} \vdots S_{N,1}S_{N,2}\dots S_{N,N} T_{1,1}T_{1,2}\dots T_{1,M} T_{2,1}T_{2,2}\dots T_{2,M} \vdots T_{M,1}T_{M,2}\dots T_{M,M} Output Print a and b in this order, separated by a space on one line. Constraints - 1 \leq M \leq N \leq 50 - N and M are integers. - Each of S_{i,j} and T_{i,j} is . or #.
